target_estimand: \(\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]})=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i^{[L,U]}(1)-[Y_i^{[L,U]}(2)+Y_i^{[L,U]}(3)]/2\}\) for a fixed complete schedule in \([L,U]^{3n}\), with the binary target \(\tau(z)\) obtained at \([L,U]=[0,1]\).
estimand_functional:
For fixed finite \(L<U\), with \(W=U-L\),
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}
=W^2\{n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\},
\qquad C_3=-a_1',
\]
and, uniformly on compact sets of \(\zeta_n=n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\),
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)
=W^2\left[n^{-1}+n^{-4/3}\{\mathsf P(\zeta_n)-C_3\}
+o(n^{-4/3})\right].
\]

sampling_model.design: The unrestricted benchmark ranges over every law on \(\mathcal A^n\) chosen independently of the fixed complete schedule; no coordinate independence or arm positivity is imposed. The attaining comparator is iid \(q^\star\), and the allocation frontier ranges over iid triangular arrays \(q_n\).
sampling_model.units: There are \(n\) labelled units with a fixed complete schedule in \([L,U]^{3n}\), where \(-\infty<L<U<\infty\) is common to all arms and units and fixed with respect to \(n\). Binary schedules are the normalized endpoint subclass; no superpopulation sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives exactly one of three labelled arms and reveals only \(Y_i^{[L,U]}(A_i)\). The target is the fixed finite-population contrast with weights \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity restriction is imposed on unrestricted competing designs. Each iid frontier array is eventually interior because it converges to \(q^\star=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisance regressions. The bounded upper rule independently Bernoulliizes normalized observed outcomes and then analytically averages that randomization, so the reported Rao--Blackwellized estimator is a deterministic function of the realized assignment and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2.1--2.2 identify the two-arm binary reduced experiment and Theorem 2.3 transfers its unrestricted minimax value exactly to a common bounded interval.
For two bounded-outcome arms, iid half assignment and a nonlinear endpoint-derived estimator attain the unrestricted minimax value characterized by a finite convex program.
Under the paper's permutation-invariant uncertainty class and linear-estimation formulation, complete randomization and a Neyman allocation solve the stated minimax problem.
For general multi-treatment finite-population contrasts and assignment mechanisms, the paper gives exact variance identities for linear unbiased estimators.
For multi-arm complete randomization with fixed limiting allocation proportions, regression-adjusted estimators admit regular design-based asymptotic comparisons.
Second-order asymptotic minimax behavior can be characterized by square completion and a problem-specific differential operator.
Restricted normal-mean minimax risk has a boundary-layer analysis based on least-favorable distributions.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population total estimation, pairwise-independent sampling and midpoint-differenced Horvitz--Thompson estimation attain the sharp minimax criterion.

tldr: For the fixed three-arm contrast \(1,-1/2,-1/2\) and any common finite outcome interval \[L,U\], an exact endpoint-transfer theorem makes the unrestricted and iid bounded minimax values \(U-L\)^2 times their binary values. The eight-type orbit game remains a literal reduction only for binary endpoint schedules. The new proved kernel identifies the half-wedge Airy constant \(C_3=-a_1^{\prime}\), establishes matching global minimax-value bounds through schedule-uniform estimators and all-design priors, and gives the sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) iid allocation frontier. A stronger fiberwise uniform liminf/recovery comparison across transverse strata remains open.

project_justification.gap: The two-arm sources and accepted binary multi-arm parent do not determine the three-arm half-wedge constant, derive its allocation frontier, or prove exact bounded endpoint transfer; a stronger transverse fiberwise experiment comparison also remains open.
project_justification.niche: For the labelled active-versus-pooled-comparators contrast, zero-sum normalization permits exact bounded endpoint transfer, while the binary endpoint adversary has genuinely three-arm half-wedge geometry and sharp global value bounds despite an unresolved stronger fiberwise comparison at eta=0.
project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-n endpoint equality, the exact half-wedge Airy constant, matching schedule-uniform and all-design global value bounds, and the necessary-and-sufficient n^(-1/6) allocation frontier. It does not claim the open fiberwise liminf/recovery theorem.

related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.1--2.2) identify the balanced two-arm binary reduced experiment, and their Theorem 2.3 proves the two-arm bounded endpoint transfer that motivates the design-preserving three-arm proof here. Their Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C inform the one-dimensional Airy correction, but do not determine the labelled three-arm half-wedge constant or singular transverse bridge. The accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) supplies the lossless labelled eight-type reduction for binary schedules only. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and proof A.4) informs two-arm endpoint-game and posterior-mean constructions. Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) supply general arm-labelled contrasts and unequal replication with linear unbiased estimation. Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) informs the first-order allocation square completion; Zhao and Ding (2023) and Li and Ding (2017) provide regular multi-arm finite-population asymptotics. Levit (1981) and Bickel (1981) inform the spectral route, while Aronow and Lopatto (2026, Theorems 1--3) impose design unbiasedness, which is not imposed here.
interpretation: Changing the measurement scale from binary endpoints to a common interval of width \(W\) multiplies every squared-error benchmark and allocation penalty by \(W^2\), but it does not change \(q^\star\), the \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation tolerance, or the dimensionless constant \(C_3\). The continuous bounded experiment is handled by Rao--Blackwellized endpoint randomization, not by pretending each bounded response is one of eight binary types.
technical_internal_limitation: The bounded transfer is an exact equality of minimax values, not a literal finite-orbit representation of each continuous schedule. The proved singular statement is only a global minimax-value sandwich: the dual prior concentrates at eta=0 and does not furnish fiberwise recovery uniformly across a transverse eta-band. The stronger liminf/recovery comparison remains open.
honest_scope: The lossless eight-type orbit reduction is inherited and literal only for binary endpoint schedules. The endpoint theorem proves exact bounded minimax-value identities and transports estimators and priors. The singular theorem proves only matching global worst-case/Bayes value inequalities; it does not prove a uniform liminf or recovery comparison over an eta-band, a transverse-stratum comparison, cellwise Le Cam equivalence, a continuous-schedule eight-type likelihood, uniqueness of the unrestricted design, equality with fixed-count complete randomization, or exact finite-n saddle attainment. The stronger fiberwise comparison remains open.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of labelled experimental units.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: \(t=(t_1,t_2,t_3)\) records one unit's three potential outcomes.

symbols.name: \mathcal T
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T=\{0,1\}^3\), containing the eight arm-labelled binary response types.

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: \(z=(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) fixes all three potential outcomes of every labelled unit before assignment.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau
symbols.def: An arbitrary measurable, possibly biased decision rule clipped to the target range.

symbols.name: R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
symbols.def: \(R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z))^2]\), with expectation only over \(A\).

symbols.name: q_n
symbols.def: The allocation vector used at population size \(n\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_q
symbols.def: Under \(\mathcal D_q\), the coordinates \(A_i\) are independent and \(\Pr(A_i=a)=q_a\).

symbols.name: \pi
symbols.def: \(\pi_r\) is the probability assigned to the uniform labelled assignment orbit with arm counts \(r\).

symbols.name: \delta

symbols.name: \mathcal H(m,r,x)

symbols.def: The probability of \(x\) under uniform labelled assignment conditional on arm counts \(r\) and schedule orbit \(m\).

symbols.name: G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)

assumptions.condition: The complete binary schedule \(z\) is fixed; probability statements condition on it.
The assignment law \(\mathcal D\) is selected without observing the relevant fixed complete schedule, whether binary \(z\) or bounded \(z^{[L,U]}\).

standard.name: Known randomized assignment independent of fixed potential outcomes

definitions.name: Binary endpoint unrestricted three-arm minimax game
definitions.construction:
The binary endpoint value is
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=\inf_{\mathcal D\in\Delta(\mathcal A^n),\,\widehat\tau:\mathcal O_n\to[-1,1]}
\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z)\}^2.
\]
Here \(\mathcal T=\{0,1\}^3\), so this definition is literally the binary endpoint game.  Its relation to a continuous bounded schedule class is a separate minimax-value identity, not a literal eight-type orbit representation of every bounded schedule.

definitions.name: Binary endpoint iid allocation minimax game
definitions.construction:
For an interior allocation vector \(q\), the binary endpoint iid value is
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=\inf_{\widehat\tau:\mathcal O_n\to[-1,1]}
\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}\mathbb E_{\mathcal D_q}\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z)\}^2.
\]
This is the iid restriction of the binary endpoint game.  The continuous bounded-schedule value is defined separately and is linked to this value by endpoint transfer rather than by treating continuous schedules as eight response types.

definitions.name: Finite orbit-game constructions
definitions.construction: Let \(\pi\) range over laws on arm-count vectors \(r\) with \(\sum_ar_a=n\), and let \(\delta(r,x)\in[-1,1]\). Define \(G_n^{\mathrm{all}}=\inf_{\pi,\delta}\max_{m\in\mathcal M_n}\sum_r\pi_r\sum_xP_m(x\mid r)\{\delta(r,x)-n^{-1}\sum_tm_t\mu(t)\}^2\). Define \(G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\) by fixing \(\pi_r=n!\prod_aq_a^{r_a}/\prod_ar_a!\).

definitions.name: Stratified face/corner spectral experiment
definitions.construction: For each fixed \(\eta\), minimize \(\mathcal E_\eta(\psi)=\int_{\mathbb R}\{4|\psi'(u)|^2+V(u,\eta)|\psi(u)|^2\}\,du\) over \(\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R)\) with \(\int\psi^2=1\). The full value is the infimum over fibers \(\eta\in\mathbb R\); the transverse dual is allowed to be a probability measure, including a point mass at \(\eta=0\).

definitions.name: Iid Airy-feedback procedure
definitions.construction: Under \(\mathcal D_q\), compute \(T_{n,q}=n^{-1}\sum_i c_{A_i}(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2)/q_{A_i}\) and report \(\delta_{n,q}=\operatorname{proj}_{[-1,1]}\{T_{n,q}-n^{-2/3}s_3(n^{1/3}T_{n,q})\}\), where \(s_3=-2\phi_3'/\phi_3\).

definitions.name: Label-preserving half-effect schedule prior
definitions.construction: Draw \(X\) with density \(f\), set \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}X\), and condition on \(|\alpha|<1/3\). Independently across labelled units draw response types according to \(p_t(\alpha)\). The induced law on complete schedules is \(\Pi_{A,n}\).

definitions.name: Allocation-regularized complete-schedule prior
definitions.construction: Draw \(V_a\) and \(U_i\) as specified, set \(P_a=1/2+\varepsilon_nV_a\), and form \(Y_i(a)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le P_a\}\); the induced complete-schedule law is \(\Pi_{B,n}\). Define \(\Pi_n=(1-n^{-1/4})\Pi_{A,n}+n^{-1/4}\Pi_{B,n}\).

definitions.name: Exact rational finite-orbit certificate
definitions.construction: Restrict each orbit decision \(\delta(r,x)\) to a mixture over \(\Gamma_M\), linearize the resulting squared risks with nonnegative joint design--action weights, and minimize their common upper bound over the design-orbit law for \(\Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{all}}\), or fix the multinomial \(q\)-law for \(\Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\).

definitions.name: Singular finite-orbit bridge handle
definitions.construction: Start from the exact likelihood \(P_m(x\mid r)\); stratify local type counts by \((\theta,\eta)\); use a discrete Stein expansion only in the target coordinate; retain zero-likelihood cells through the primal risk inequalities; compactify duals as probability measures in \(\eta\) with fiberwise \(H^1\) control in \(\theta\); and construct liminf and recovery comparisons uniform on shrinking neighborhoods of \(\eta=0\).

definitions.name: Bounded three-arm minimax games
definitions.construction:
Fix finite endpoints \(L<U\) and write \(W=U-L\).  A bounded complete schedule is
\(z^{[L,U]}=(Y_i^{[L,U]}(a))_{i,a}\in[L,U]^{3n}\), it produces
\(Y_i^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i^{[L,U]}(A_i)\), and its causal contrast is
\[
\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]})
=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}c_aY_i^{[L,U]}(a).
\]
Because \(\sum_ac_a=0\), \(\sum_{a:c_a>0}c_a=1\), and
\(\sum_{a:c_a<0}|c_a|=1\), this target lies in \([-W,W]\).  Let
\(\mathcal O_{n,[L,U]}=(\mathcal A\times[L,U])^n\), let
\(\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}:\mathcal O_{n,[L,U]}\to[-W,W]\), and define
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau_{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]})
=\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\left[
\left\{\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}-\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]})\right\}^2\right].
\]
The bounded unrestricted and iid minimax values are
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}
=\inf_{\mathcal D,\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}}
\sup_{z^{[L,U]}\in[L,U]^{3n}}
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau_{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]}),
\]
and
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
=\inf_{\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}}
\sup_{z^{[L,U]}\in[L,U]^{3n}}
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D_q,\widehat\tau_{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]}).
\]
The assignment law is selected independently of the fixed bounded schedule, exactly as in the binary game.

definitions.name: Rao--Blackwellized bounded estimator and endpoint prior
definitions.construction:
Fix finite \(L<U\), put \(W=U-L\), and let observed data be generated from the fixed schedule under \(\mathcal D_q\).  Conditional on the realized bounded data, generate independent auxiliary variables
\[
B_i\mid A,Y_i^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}}
\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\left(
\frac{Y_i^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}}-L}{W}\right),\qquad 1\leq i\leq n.
\]
The Rao--Blackwellized bounded Airy rule is
\[
\delta_{n,q}^{[L,U]}(A,Y^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}})
=W\,\mathbb E_B\left[
\delta_{n,q}\bigl((A_i,B_i)_{i=1}^n\bigr)
\mathrel{}\middle|\mathrel{} A,Y^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}}
\right].
\]
It takes values in \([-W,W]\).  The bounded endpoint prior
\(\Pi_n^{[L,U]}\) is the pushforward of \(\Pi_n\) under the coordinatewise map
\(t_{i,a}\mapsto L+Wt_{i,a}\).  Thus it is a prior on fixed complete bounded schedules supported on the endpoints \(\{L,U\}^{3n}\).

statements.statement: Import the lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit-game reduction established in the accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\). For every \(n\), common permutation symmetrization identifies \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=G_n^{\mathrm{all}},\qquad \rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q).\] Its exact likelihood is \(P_m(x\mid r)\), and its attained finite primal and dual games retain zero arm counts and zero-likelihood observation cells.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(G=\mathfrak S_n\) act simultaneously on schedules, assignments, and observed outcome vectors by permuting unit labels.  Fix a schedule-independent procedure with assignment pmf \(p(a)=\mathcal D(a)\) and deterministic estimator \(\delta(a,y)\in[-1,1]\).  Draw \(\sigma\) uniformly from \(G\), draw \(B\sim p\), assign \(A=\sigma B\), and after observing \(y\) report the randomized action
\[
D=\delta(\sigma^{-1}A,\sigma^{-1}y).
\]
Under a fixed schedule \(z\), inverse-permuting the observed data gives exactly the data generated by the original procedure under \(\sigma^{-1}z\).  Since \(\tau(\sigma^{-1}z)=\tau(z)\),
\[
\mathbb E_z\{D-\tau(z)\}^2
=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{\sigma\in G}
R_n(\mathcal D,\delta;\sigma^{-1}z).
\tag{1}
\]

The marginal symmetrized assignment law is
\[
\bar p(a)=\frac1{|G|}\sum_{\sigma\in G}p(\sigma^{-1}a).
\]
When \(\bar p(a)>0\), define the assignment-conditioned weights and deterministic action
\[
w_\sigma(a)=\frac{p(\sigma^{-1}a)}{\sum_{\gamma\in G}p(\gamma^{-1}a)},
\qquad
\bar\delta(a,y)=\sum_{\sigma\in G}w_\sigma(a)
\delta(\sigma^{-1}a,\sigma^{-1}y).
\tag{2}
\]
The weights depend only on the realized assignment \(A=a\), not on \(y\) or the unknown schedule \(z\).  The action space \([-1,1]\) is convex, so \(\bar\delta(a,y)\in[-1,1]\).  If \(\bar p(a)=0\), invariance of \(\bar p\) makes the entire assignment orbit null; define \(\bar\delta\) there arbitrarily, say zero.  Formula (2) is the conditional mean of \(D\) given \(A=a\) in the randomized construction, with \(y\) held at its realized value.  Conditional Jensen and (1) therefore give, for every fixed schedule,
\[
R_n(\bar{\mathcal D},\bar\delta;z)
\leq\frac1{|G|}\sum_{\sigma\in G}
R_n(\mathcal D,\delta;\sigma^{-1}z)
\leq\max_{z'\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D,\delta;z').
\tag{3}
\]
A change of summation variable shows that \(\bar p(\eta a)=\bar p(a)\) and \(\bar\delta(\eta a,\eta y)=\bar\delta(a,y)\) for every \(\eta\in G\).  Thus one schedule-independent deterministic invariant rule suffices, including on null assignment orbits.

An invariant assignment law is constant on each orbit of \(\mathcal A^n\).  An orbit is indexed by \(r\), contains \(n!/\prod_a r_a!\) assignments, and hence an invariant law is uniquely a mixture \(\pi\) of uniform laws on these orbits.  An observed binary labelled array has orbit invariant \((r,x)\), so an invariant deterministic action is precisely \(\delta(r,x)\).  Likewise, two complete schedules are in the same orbit exactly when their eight type counts \(m\) agree, so maximization over schedules becomes maximization over \(\mathcal M_n\).

Fix \(m,r,x\).  For each \(h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)\), the number of labelled assignments producing \(h\) is
\[
\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}\frac{m_t!}{\prod_{a\in\mathcal A}h_{t,a}!}.
\]
Dividing their sum by the orbit size gives exactly the likelihood in \(\textnormal{def:orbit-likelihood}\):
\[
P_m(x\mid r)=\frac{\prod_a r_a!}{n!}
\sum_{h\in\mathcal H(m,r,x)}
\prod_{t\in\mathcal T}\frac{m_t!}{\prod_a h_{t,a}!}.
\]
Substitution into the invariant risk gives \(G_n^{\mathrm{all}}\), proving \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=G_n^{\mathrm{all}}\).  Under \(\mathcal D_q\), independence gives
\[
\pi_r=\frac{n!}{\prod_a r_a!}\prod_aq_a^{r_a},
\]
so the same substitution gives \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\).  The state spaces are finite and the action interval is compact, so all decision minima are attained.  No argument deletes an orbit with \(r_a=0\); when \(P_m(x\mid r)=0\), its summand is zero while the corresponding primal cell remains in the finite game.

statements.statement: The six response types outside \(\{000,111\}\) have \((\mu(t),\nu(t),\mu(t)^2)\) equal to \((-1/2,-1,1/4)\), \((-1/2,1,1/4)\), \((-1,0,1)\), \((1,0,1)\), \((1/2,-1,1/4)\), and \((1/2,1,1/4)\). Consequently the tangent program has the exact value \[V(\theta,\eta)=\max\{|\theta|/2,|\eta|/4\}.\] Integer response-type counts recover every compact set of local coordinates with \(O(n^{-2/3})\) coordinate and cost error.
statements.justification: The polyhedral potential is the first mathematical step that differs from the published scalar two-arm boundary.
statements.gap: The two-arm potential in Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Section 3) is \(|\theta|\); no cited work derives this labelled face/corner support function.
statements.consumer: The explicit potential identifies which complete schedules drive second-order risk and makes the proposed constant numerically and analytically evaluable.
statements.proof_tex:
Direct substitution in \(\mu(t)=t_1-(t_2+t_3)/2\) and \(\nu(t)=t_2-t_3\) gives, in the order \(001,010,011,100,101,110\),
\[
(\mu,\nu,\mu^2)
=(-1/2,-1,1/4),\,(-1/2,1,1/4),\,(-1,0,1),\,
  (1,0,1),\,(1/2,-1,1/4),\,(1/2,1,1/4).
\]
Every one of these six triples satisfies
\[
 \mu(t)^2\geq \frac{|\mu(t)|}{2},
 \qquad
 \mu(t)^2\geq \frac{|\nu(t)|}{4}.
\]
Consequently every feasible \(\lambda\) in the tangent program satisfies, by the triangle inequality,
\[
\sum_t\lambda_t\mu(t)^2\geq\frac{|\theta|}{2},
\qquad
\sum_t\lambda_t\mu(t)^2\geq\frac{|\eta|}{4}.
\]

For the reverse inequality put \(S=\max\{2|\theta|,|\eta|\}\).  If \(S=0\), take all four masses below equal to zero.  If \(S>0\), for \(\sigma,\tau\in\{-1,1\}\) assign to the half-effect type having \((\mu,\nu)=(\sigma/2,\tau)\) the mass
\[
 \lambda_{\sigma,\tau}
 =\frac S4\left(1+\sigma\frac{2\theta}{S}\right)
             \left(1+\tau\frac{\eta}{S}\right).
\]
These masses are nonnegative, their \(\mu\)-sum is \(\theta\), their \(\nu\)-sum is \(\eta\), and their total mass is \(S\).  Since every such type has cost \(1/4\), the achieved cost is
\[
 \frac S4=\max\left\{\frac{|\theta|}{2},\frac{|\eta|}{4}\right\}.
\]
This proves the exact formula for \(V\).

Finally, on a compact coordinate set the four displayed masses are uniformly bounded.  Round each \(n^{2/3}\lambda_{\sigma,\tau}\) to a nonnegative integer and put all unused units in type \(000\).  Each of the two coordinates and the scaled cost changes by at most a constant times \(n^{-2/3}\), uniformly on that compact set; for all sufficiently large \(n\) the reservoir count is nonnegative.  This gives the asserted integer recovery along the full integer sequence.

statements.statement: Under \(\Pi_{A,n}\), conditional on \(\alpha\) and any assignment vector, the signed observations \(\operatorname{sign}(c_{A_i})(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\) are independent with success probability \((1+\alpha)/2\), while the posterior mean of \(\tau(z)\) retains the arm-labelled coefficient \(b_{A_i}(\alpha)\). For \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}u\), the generalized information inequality and conditional-residual term give, uniformly over every schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), the second-order coefficient \[I(f)+\{2\bar q_1(\mathcal D)-1/2\}m_1(f),\] up to \(o(1)\). The cusp at \(\alpha=0\) has cancelling traces and creates no extra boundary term.
statements.justification: This coefficient is the early kill test: omitting the label-dependent posterior target or its residual variance changes the proposed potential and constant.
statements.gap: The published two-arm lower bound uses a scalar target and symmetric least-favorable prior; it has no arm-labelled posterior coefficient or allocation-sensitive residual term.
statements.consumer: The exact coefficient supplies a trustworthy lower-bound diagnostic before the singular experiment-convergence argument is attempted.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(s=|\alpha|\), \(\alpha_+=\max(\alpha,0)\), and \(\alpha_-=\max(-\alpha,0)\).  The six displayed nonzero probabilities in \(\textnormal{def:half-effect-prior}\) are nonnegative for \(|\alpha|<1/3\) and sum to one.  Direct enumeration gives
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha\mu(t)=\alpha,
\qquad
\mathbb E_\alpha\mu(t)^2=\frac{s}{2},
\]
and
\[
\Pr_\alpha\{Y(1)=1\}=\frac{1+\alpha}{2},
\qquad
\Pr_\alpha\{Y(2)=1\}=\Pr_\alpha\{Y(3)=1\}=\frac{1-\alpha}{2}.
\]
Let \(Z_i=\operatorname{sign}(c_{A_i})(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\).  Conditional on \((\alpha,A)\), schedule independence and the product construction of \(\Pi_{A,n}\) imply that the \(Z_i\) are independent and
\[
\Pr_\alpha(Z_i=1\mid A)=\frac{1+\alpha}{2}
\]
for every arm label.

Because a binary \(Z\in\{-1,1\}\) has an affine conditional regression, its regression is determined by its mean and covariance.  Here \(\mathbb E_\alpha Z=\alpha\), while enumeration gives
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha\{\mu(t)Z\mid A=1\}=|\alpha|,
\qquad
\mathbb E_\alpha\{\mu(t)Z\mid A=2\}
=\mathbb E_\alpha\{\mu(t)Z\mid A=3\}=0.
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha\{\mu(t_i)\mid A_i=a,Z_i\}
=\alpha+b_a(\alpha)(Z_i-\alpha),
\]
with precisely the declared coefficients \(b_a(\alpha)\).  Conditional independence across units yields
\[
g(\alpha,A,Z):=\mathbb E_\alpha\{\tau(z)\mid A,Z\}
=\alpha+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n b_{A_i}(\alpha)(Z_i-\alpha)
\]
and the conditional-residual identity
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha\operatorname{Var}\{\tau(z)\mid\alpha,A,Z\}
=\frac{s/2-\alpha^2}{n}
-\frac{1-\alpha^2}{n^2}\,
\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}\sum_{i=1}^n b_{A_i}(\alpha)^2.
\tag{1}
\]

Differentiate \(g\) at fixed \((A,Z)\) separately on the two half-lines.  Since \(\mathbb E_\alpha(Z_i-\alpha)=0\),
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha\{\partial_\alpha g(\alpha,A,Z)\}
=1-\sum_a\bar q_a(\mathcal D)b_a(\alpha)
=1-\frac{\bar q_1(\mathcal D)|\alpha|-\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2}.
\tag{2}
\]
The two formulas for \(g\) have the same trace at zero.  Hence integration by parts on \((-1/3,0)\) and \((0,1/3)\) produces opposite traces at zero, which cancel.

Let \(\varpi_n(\alpha)=n^{1/3}f(n^{1/3}\alpha)\), let \(\ell_\alpha(A,Z)\) be the conditional likelihood, and set
\[
S_\alpha=\partial_\alpha\log\{\varpi_n(\alpha)\ell_\alpha(A,Z)\}.
\]
The compact support of \(f\), the cancellation just proved, and integration by parts give, for every estimator \(D(A,Z)\),
\[
\mathbb E\{(D-g)S_\alpha\}=\mathbb E(\partial_\alpha g).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz therefore yields
\[
\mathbb E(D-g)^2\geq
\frac{\{\mathbb E(\partial_\alpha g)\}^2}{\mathbb E S_\alpha^2}.
\tag{3}
\]
The prior-likelihood score cross term has mean zero, and the Bernoulli likelihood information is \(n/(1-\alpha^2)\).  Therefore
\[
\mathbb E S_\alpha^2
=n^{2/3}I(f)+n\,\mathbb E\frac1{1-\alpha^2}.
\tag{4}
\]
With \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}u\), compact support permits Taylor expansion uniformly over every \(\bar q(\mathcal D)\in\Delta_3\):
\[
\{\mathbb E(\partial_\alpha g)\}^2
=1-2\bar q_1(\mathcal D)n^{-1/3}m_1(f)+O_f(n^{-2/3}),
\]
\[
\{\mathbb E S_\alpha^2\}^{-1}
=\frac1n-I(f)n^{-4/3}+O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{5}
\]
Equation (1) contributes
\[
\frac12m_1(f)n^{-4/3}+O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{6}
\]
Combining (3)--(6) with total conditional variance proves, uniformly over schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\),
\[
\inf_D\mathbb E(D-\tau)^2
\geq \frac1n-n^{-4/3}
\left[I(f)+\{2\bar q_1(\mathcal D)-1/2\}m_1(f)\right]
+O_f(n^{-5/3}),
\]
which is the claimed coefficient, including the arm-labelled posterior term and the conditional residual.

statements.statement: The stratified face/corner experiment has value \[\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\inf_{\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R):\int\psi^2=1}\mathcal E_\eta(\psi)=\inf_{\psi:\int\psi^2=1}\int_{\mathbb R}\{4|\psi'(u)|^2+|u||\psi(u)|^2/2\}\,du=C_3.\] The least fiber is \(\eta=0\); \(\phi_3\) is its positive even ground state, satisfies \(\phi_3'(0)=0\), and has eigenvalue \(C_3=-a_1'\). Along the full integer sequence, the imported exact orbit games obey \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\qquad \rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)=\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Thus iid \(q^\star\) is second-order minimax and \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)-\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}=o(n^{-4/3})\). The new assertion is the exact half-wedge constant and its uniform transfer through the singular labelled finite experiment; the orbit equality itself is inherited infrastructure.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\textnormal{lem:tangent-half-wedge}\) and \(\textnormal{def:face-corner-energy}\),
\[
V(u,\eta)=\max\{|u|/2,|\eta|/4\}\geq |u|/2.
\]
The Airy fiber calculus then gives
\[
\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\inf_{\substack{\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R)\\ \int\psi^2=1}}
\mathcal E_\eta(\psi)
=\inf_{\substack{\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R)\\ \int\psi^2=1}}
\int_{\mathbb R}\left\{4|\psi'(u)|^2+\frac{|u|}{2}|\psi(u)|^2\right\}\,du
=C_3,
\]
with equality at \(\eta=0\).  The same lemma identifies the normalized minimizer as \(\phi_3(u)\propto\operatorname{Ai}(|u|/2-C_3)\), gives \(\phi_3'(0)=0\), and hence gives \(\operatorname{Ai}'(-C_3)=0\).  Positivity of the ground state and the declared ordering of Airy derivative zeros select the largest negative zero, so \(C_3=-a_1'\).

The matching finite-\(n\) construction gives
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)
\leq \frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{7}
\]
Because the unrestricted design class contains \(\mathcal D_{q^\star}\),
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}\leq\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star).
\tag{8}
\]
For every schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), the prior part of \(\textnormal{prop:matching-finite-n-constructions}\) gives
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau}\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_n}
R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
\geq \frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\tag{9}
\]
uniformly in \(\mathcal D\).  A maximum over \(\mathcal T^n\) dominates its average under \(\Pi_n\).  Taking the estimator infimum and then the design infimum in (9) yields
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}}
\geq \frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{10}
\]
Equations (7)--(10) prove the two displayed risk expansions.  Their difference is \(o(n^{-4/3})\).  Finally, \(\textnormal{thm:uniform-singular-value-bridge}\) records exactly the same two global worst-case and Bayes value bounds used in (7)--(10), including all zero-likelihood cells and dormant constraints.  No fiberwise, transverse, or cellwise experiment comparison is used.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the exact nonlinear binary endpoint gain; the proved bounded corollary transfers that gain, with squared-width scaling, to every common finite interval.
statements.gap: The published two-arm theory gives neither the three-arm half-wedge eigenvalue \(-a_1'\) nor the singular labelled finite-orbit bridge; its bounded theorem also does not itself establish the three-arm transfer.
statements.consumer: For an active treatment compared with two equally weighted comparators, the binary theorem and bounded corollary give the sharp worst-case MSE benchmark on any known common outcome interval.

statements.statement: Let \((q_n)\) be iid allocation vectors with \(q_n\to q^\star\). Uniformly whenever \(\zeta_n=n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\) ranges over a compact subset of \(\{v:v_1+v_2+v_3=0\}\), \[\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)=\frac1n+n^{-4/3}\{\mathsf P(\zeta_n)-C_3\}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] Hence an iid allocation array retains the unrestricted sharp correction \(C_3\) if and only if \(n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\to0\). If \(q_n\to q^\star\) and \(n^{1/6}\|q_n-q^\star\|\to\infty\), then \(n^{4/3}\{\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-n^{-1}\}\to\infty\). The penalty \(\mathsf P(\zeta)=2\zeta_1^2+4\zeta_2^2+4\zeta_3^2\) is the constrained Hessian of \(q\mapsto\frac14\sum_ac_a^2/q_a\), and the displayed expansion proves its uniform coupling to the half-wedge experiment.
statements.proof_tex:
Define
\[
F(q)=\frac14\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2}{q_a}.
\]
Directly from \(\textnormal{def:airy-feedback-procedure}\), for every fixed schedule,
\[
\mathbb ET_{n,q}=\tau(z),
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(T_{n,q})
=\frac{F(q)}n-\frac1{n^2}\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2.
\tag{11}
\]
For \(q\) in a fixed neighborhood of the interior point \(q^\star\), the independent centered summands are uniformly bounded, whence their averaged third absolute moment is \(O(n^{-3/2})\).  Put
\[
A_n=n^{-2/3}\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2,
\qquad x=n^{1/3}\tau(z).
\]
Taylor expansion using the bounded Lipschitz derivatives supplied by \(\textnormal{lem:airy-fiber-calculus}\) gives, uniformly in the schedule,
\[
R_n(\mathcal D_q,\delta_{n,q};z)
=\frac{F(q)}n+n^{-4/3}
\left[-A_n-2F(q)s_3'(x)+s_3(x)^2
+2n^{-1/3}A_ns_3'(x)\right]+O(n^{-3/2}).
\tag{12}
\]
Indeed, the cross-term remainder is bounded by a constant times \(n^{-2/3}n^{2/3}\mathbb E|T_{n,q}-\tau(z)|^3=O(n^{-3/2})\), and the square remainder is no larger because \(s_3^2\) is Lipschitz.

The response-type list in \(\textnormal{lem:tangent-half-wedge}\) gives \(\mu(t)^2\geq|\mu(t)|/2\).  Thus
\[
A_n\geq |x|/2,
\qquad 0\leq A_n\leq n^{1/3}.
\tag{13}
\]
The constrained gradient of \(F\) vanishes at \(q^\star\), so \(q-q^\star=O(n^{-1/6})\) implies
\[
F(q)-1=O(n^{-1/3}).
\tag{14}
\]
Using the Riccati identity \(s_3^2-2s_3'=|x|/2-C_3\), equations (12)--(14), and \(|s_3'(x)|\leq K(1+|x|)^{-1/2}\), we obtain
\[
\max_zR_n(\mathcal D_q,\delta_{n,q};z)
\leq\frac{F(q)}n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\tag{15}
\]
uniformly on compact sets of \(n^{1/6}(q-q^\star)\).  Projection cannot increase squared distance from \(\tau(z)\in[-1,1]\).  The reverse inequality in (15) is \(\textnormal{lem:q-dependent-half-effect-bound}\), hence
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)
=\frac{F(q_n)}n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{16}
\]

Write \(d=q-q^\star\), where \(d_1+d_2+d_3=0\).  Taylor expansion at the interior point \(q^\star\) gives, with a uniform cubic remainder,
\[
F(q^\star+d)
=1+2d_1^2+4d_2^2+4d_3^2+O(\|d\|^3).
\tag{17}
\]
Substituting \(d=n^{-1/6}\zeta_n\) into (16)--(17) proves the asserted uniform expansion with penalty \(\mathsf P\).

If \(\zeta_n\to0\), the expansion matches the unrestricted coefficient \(-C_3\) from \(\textnormal{thm:sharp-face-corner-expansion}\).  Conversely, suppose \(\zeta_n\not\to0\).  If \((\zeta_n)\) is bounded, there are \(\varepsilon>0\) and a subsequence with \(\|\zeta_n\|\geq\varepsilon\); a further subsequence converges to a nonzero \(\zeta\), and positive definiteness of \(\mathsf P\) gives a coefficient different from \(-C_3\).  If \((\zeta_n)\) is unbounded, choose a subsequence along which \(\|\zeta_n\|\to\infty\).  Along this subsequence the second bound in \(\textnormal{lem:q-dependent-half-effect-bound}\) and strong convexity of \(F\) near \(q^\star\) give constants \(k,K>0\) such that
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-\frac1n\right\}
\geq k n^{1/3}\|q_n-q^\star\|^2-K
=k\|\zeta_n\|^2-K\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus every array that does not converge to zero has a subsequence incompatible with retaining the sharp correction, including arrays that are unbounded but do not diverge in norm.  This proves the necessary-and-sufficient frontier.  If the full array satisfies \(\|\zeta_n\|\to\infty\), the same displayed lower bound holds along the full sequence and proves the theorem's final divergence assertion.
statements.justification: This necessary-and-sufficient frontier turns the design into a first-class object and quantifies exactly when allocation error erases the second-order minimax gain.
statements.gap: Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) gives a first-order quadratic allocation result for linear procedures, while Zhao and Ding (2023) hold limiting multi-arm proportions fixed; neither derives the \(n^{-1/6}\) threshold or couples it to nonlinear minimax risk.
statements.consumer: A multi-arm trial can translate the theorem into an allocation-tolerance rule: deviations smaller than \(n^{-1/6}\) preserve the sharp gain, while local deviations incur the explicit penalty.

statements.statement: At \(q=q^\star\), the explicit estimator \(\delta_{n,q^\star}\) satisfies \[\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D_{q^\star},\delta_{n,q^\star};z)\le n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\] uniformly over complete schedules. The explicit prior \(\Pi_n\) satisfies, uniformly over every schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), \[\inf_{\widehat\tau}\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_n}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)\ge n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).\] The broad component yields a positive quadratic coercivity term in \(\|\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\|\); completing the square against the linear half-effect-prior term contributes only \(o(n^{-4/3})\). Finally, with \(M=n\), both rational grid programs bracket their continuous orbit games within \(1/(4n^2)=o(n^{-4/3})\).
statements.proof_tex:
At \(q=q^\star\), the identity \(c_a/q_a^\star=2\operatorname{sign}(c_a)\) gives
\[
T_{n,q^\star}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n W_i,
\qquad
W_i=\operatorname{sign}(c_{A_i})(2Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1)\in\{-1,1\}.
\]
For a fixed schedule, iid assignment makes the \(W_i\) independent and direct summation over arms gives
\[
\mathbb EW_i=\mu(t_i),
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(T_{n,q^\star})
=\frac1n-\frac1{n^2}\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2.
\tag{18}
\]
Put \(Q=\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2\), \(A_n=Q/n^{2/3}\), \(x=n^{1/3}\tau(z)\), and \(\varepsilon=T_{n,q^\star}-\tau(z)\).  Bounded independence gives \(\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^3=O(n^{-3/2})\), uniformly in \(z\).  Taylor expansion using the regularity in \(\textnormal{lem:airy-fiber-calculus}\) yields
\[
\mathbb E\left[
\varepsilon-n^{-2/3}s_3\{x+n^{1/3}\varepsilon\}
\right]^2
=\frac1n+n^{-4/3}
\left[-A_n-2(1-Q/n)s_3'(x)+s_3(x)^2\right]
+O(n^{-3/2}).
\tag{19}
\]
The cross-term remainder is bounded by a constant times \(n^{-2/3}n^{2/3}\mathbb E|\varepsilon|^3\), and the squared-feedback remainder is no larger because \(s_3^2\) is Lipschitz.

Every binary response type satisfies \(\mu(t)^2\geq|\mu(t)|/2\), so
\[
A_n\geq |x|/2,
\qquad 0\leq A_n\leq n^{1/3}.
\tag{20}
\]
The Riccati identity converts the bracket in (19) to
\[
-A_n+\frac{|x|}{2}-C_3+2n^{-1/3}A_ns_3'(x).
\tag{21}
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), boundedness of \(s_3'\) makes (21) decreasing in \(A_n\).  Its maximum under (20) is attained at \(A_n=|x|/2\), while
\[
n^{-1/3}|x|\,|s_3'(x)|
\leq K n^{-1/3}|x|(1+|x|)^{-1/2}=O(n^{-1/6})
\]
because \(|x|\leq n^{1/3}\).  Projection onto \([-1,1]\) cannot increase squared distance from \(\tau(z)\in[-1,1]\).  Equations (18)--(21) prove the uniform upper bound.

For the lower construction, \(\textnormal{lem:label-preserving-bayes-expansion}\) gives
\[
B_{A,n}(\mathcal D)\geq
\frac1n-n^{-4/3}
\left[I(f)+\frac12m_1(f)+2m_1(f)
\{\bar q_1(\mathcal D)-1/2\}\right]+O_f(n^{-5/3}),
\tag{22}
\]
and \(\textnormal{lem:broad-prior-coercivity}\) gives
\[
B_{B,n}(\mathcal D)\geq
\frac{1+k\|\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\|^2}{n}-Kn^{-9/8}.
\tag{23}
\]
Bayes risk is concave in the prior because it is an infimum of linear risk functionals.  With \(\gamma_n=n^{-1/4}\) and \(d=\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\), the mixture prior therefore satisfies
\[
B_{\Pi_n}(\mathcal D)\geq
\frac1n-\{I(f)+m_1(f)/2\}n^{-4/3}
+k n^{-5/4}\|d\|^2
-2m_1(f)n^{-4/3}d_1
-O_f(n^{-11/8})-O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{24}
\]
The exact square completion is
\[
k n^{-5/4}\|d\|^2-2m_1(f)n^{-4/3}d_1
\geq-\frac{m_1(f)^2}{k}n^{-17/12}
=o(n^{-4/3}).
\tag{25}
\]
Choose smooth compactly supported even densities by cutting off and smoothing \(\phi_3^2\).  The Airy variational identity gives \(I(f)+m_1(f)/2\to C_3\).  A diagonal cutoff sequence makes this approximation and the remainders in (24) jointly \(o(n^{-4/3})\), uniformly in \(\mathcal D\).  Equations (24)--(25) prove the prior lower bound.

Finally, \(\textnormal{lem:grid-randomization-bound}\) with \(M=n\) gives
\[
0\leq\Lambda_{n,n}^{\mathrm{all}}-G_n^{\mathrm{all}}\leq\frac1{4n^2},
\qquad
0\leq\Lambda_{n,n}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)-G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)\leq\frac1{4n^2}.
\]
Since \(n^{-2}=o(n^{-4/3})\), these are the asserted finite rational brackets.
statements.justification: The proposition makes the asymptotic saddle operational and prevents the sharp value from resting on an unattained formal operator.
statements.gap: The two-arm paper constructs a scalar feedback rule and scalar Airy-squared priors; the proposed constructions must preserve arm labels and regularize every dependent assignment law without changing the second-order coefficient.
statements.consumer: The estimator is directly implementable under iid \(q^\star\), while the rational certificates allow exact finite-sample auditing of its worst-case risk.

statements.statement: On the restricted schedule class \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) for every \(i\), pool assignment labels \(2\) and \(3\). Under \(q^\star\), the resulting observation has balanced two-arm assignment, the target becomes \(n^{-1}\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(2)\}\), and the exact orbit likelihood reduces to the shifted-binomial experiment of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorem 2.1). Its restricted-class second-order constant is \(-4^{1/3}a_1'\), providing the required two-arm sanity reduction without asserting that this restricted constant equals \(C_3\).
statements.justification: The reduction verifies the normalization and distinguishes the new worst-case three-arm geometry from an embedded two-arm submodel.
statements.gap: The published scalar experiment supplies the known special case but does not establish how the unrestricted eight-type adversary lowers the constant to \(C_3\).
statements.consumer: The identity provides a regression test for symbolic and numerical implementations of the eight-type likelihood.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\) and denote their common value by \(Y_i(0)\).  Under \(q^\star\),
\[
\Pr(A_i=1)=\frac12,
\qquad
\Pr(A_i\in\{2,3\})=\frac12.
\]
After mapping labels \(2,3\) to \(0\), the assignments are iid balanced two-arm assignments.  The split between labels \(2\) and \(3\) is ancillary conditional on the pooled label because the corresponding potential outcomes coincide.  Moreover,
\[
\tau(z)=\frac1n\sum_i\left\{Y_i(1)-\frac{Y_i(2)+Y_i(3)}2\right\}
=\frac1n\sum_i\{Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)\}.
\]
In the exact orbit likelihood, summing over all splits \(r_2+r_3=r_0\) and their latent-table columns leaves the hypergeometric count for assignment to the pooled arm.  The declared published two-arm orbit reduction therefore identifies the invariant kernel with the shifted-binomial experiment.  The declared sharp two-arm theorem gives the coefficient \(-4^{1/3}a_1'\).  Because \(C_3=-a_1'\), this restricted coefficient differs from \(C_3\), as claimed.

statements.statement: Can one construct a uniform liminf and recovery comparison between the exact eight-type orbit games and the stratified face/corner experiment, with risk error \(o(n^{-4/3})\), simultaneously for \(|\eta|\le\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{bridge}}\), the coalesced fiber \(\eta=0\), every mixture on the \(000\)--\(111\) nuisance edge, every zero-likelihood observation cell, and every dormant finite-game primal constraint? The comparison must justify measure-valued concentration on \(\eta=0\), continuity of the fiber wavefunction and its \(\theta\)-derivative at \(\theta=\pm|\eta|/2\), and absence of an artificial \(\eta\)-diffusion or \(\eta\)-boundary condition.
statements.justification: This is the genuine unresolved proof boundary separating a compelling formal constant from a theorem valid for the full labelled finite experiment.
statements.gap: Appendix C of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) controls a one-dimensional lattice, while the prior orbit proposal permits arbitrary versions on null cells; neither result supplies uniform singular-fiber recovery.
statements.consumer: Closing the bridge validates the sharp constant, the allocation frontier, and the finite certificates simultaneously; failure pinpoints the first labelled orbit that requires a different limit experiment.

obligation.what_is_open: A full fiberwise primal-and-dual recovery theorem uniformly for every |eta| <= epsilon_n^bridge, beyond the proved global minimax-value comparison.
obligation.obstruction: The available dual construction is least-favorable and concentrates at eta=0; it does not furnish dual recovery uniformly across the entire eta band. The value-level theorem is sufficient for every current binary and bounded headline.
obligation.attempted: A solver wrapper was rejected after high-effort adjudication because it only cited thm:uniform-singular-value-bridge and overstated eta-uniformity. Do not dispatch this residual again unless a future directive supplies a genuinely fiberwise dual construction.
obligation.partial_result: thm:uniform-singular-value-bridge proves the required two-sided global minimax-value transfer, with primal control uniform over complete schedules and a dual prior concentrating at eta=0, while retaining null cells and dormant constraints.

statements.statement: The Airy function \(\operatorname{Ai}\) is the real solution of \(y''(x)=xy(x)\) that decays at \(+\infty\); its largest derivative zero \(a_1'\) is simple, \(\operatorname{Ai}(x)>0\) for \(x\geq a_1'\), and the standard Airy asymptotics imply \(-\operatorname{Ai}'(x)/\operatorname{Ai}(x)=x^{1/2}+O(x^{-1})\) as \(x\to+\infty\).

source.verbatim_statement: Standard properties of the Airy function [Olv97] show that Ai is C², Ai(z) > 0, Ai′(z) ≤ 0 for all z ≥ a₁′, and the following asymptotics: Ai(x)=x⁻¹ᐟ⁴/(2√π)e⁻²ˣ³ᐟ²⁄³(1+O(x⁻³ᐟ²)), Ai′(x)=−x¹ᐟ⁴/(2√π)e⁻²ˣ³ᐟ²⁄³(1+O(x⁻³ᐟ²)). By the definition of the Airy function, Ai′′(z)=zAi(z) for z∈R. The properties Ai(z)>0, Ai′(z)<0 for all z>a₁′ show that h_A is positive for t>0. Dividing immediately gives m(x):=−Ai′(x)/Ai(x)=x¹ᐟ²+O(x⁻¹), x→∞.

statements.statement:
For every \(\eta\in\mathbb R\), the fiber form in \(\mathcal E_\eta\) has a lowest eigenvalue, and
\[
\inf_{\eta\in\mathbb R}\inf_{\psi\in H^1(\mathbb R):\,\int\psi^2=1}
\mathcal E_\eta(\psi)=C_3.
\]
At \(\eta=0\) the normalized minimizer is \(\phi_3\); it is positive and even, solves
\[
-4\phi_3''(u)+\frac{|u|}{2}\phi_3(u)=C_3\phi_3(u),
\qquad \phi_3'(0)=0,
\]
and \(s_3=-2\phi_3'/\phi_3\) obeys
\[
s_3(u)^2-2s_3'(u)=\frac{|u|}{2}-C_3.
\]
Moreover \(s_3'\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(s_3^2\) is Lipschitz, and
\[
|s_3'(u)|\leq K(1+|u|)^{-1/2}
\]
for a finite constant \(K\).
statements.proof_tex:
The tangent calculation gives
\[
V(u,\eta)=\max\{|u|/2,|\eta|/4\}\geq |u|/2=V(u,0).
\]
Thus every fiber energy dominates the \(\eta=0\) energy, while \(\eta=0\) is admissible, so the infimum over fibers equals the bottom of
\[
H_0=-4\frac{d^2}{du^2}+\frac{|u|}{2}.
\]
Put \(C=-a_1'\) and \(\phi(u)=\operatorname{Ai}(|u|/2-C)\).  The cited Airy facts make \(\phi\) positive and square-integrable.  On \(u>0\),
\[
-4\phi''(u)+\frac u2\phi(u)
=-\operatorname{Ai}''(u/2-C)+\frac u2\operatorname{Ai}(u/2-C)
=C\phi(u),
\]
and the same identity holds on \(u<0\).  Since \(\operatorname{Ai}'(-C)=0\), the even extension has \(\phi'(0)=0\) and no distributional point mass in \(\phi''\).

For \(\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\), integration by parts on the two half-lines, with the boundary terms at zero cancelling because \(\phi'\) has common zero trace, yields the ground-state identity
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\left\{4|\psi'|^2+
\left(\frac{|u|}{2}-C\right)|\psi|^2\right\}du
=4\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(u)^2
\left|\left(\frac{\psi}{\phi}\right)'(u)\right|^2du\geq0.
\]
Density extends this inequality to \(H^1(\mathbb R)\).  Equality holds for the normalized \(\phi\), proving that the lowest value is \(C=C_3\) and that \(\phi_3\) is the normalized ground state.

Dividing the eigenvalue equation by \(\phi_3\) and differentiating the logarithm gives
\[
s_3^2-2s_3'=4\frac{\phi_3''}{\phi_3}
=\frac{|u|}{2}-C_3.
\]
On each half-line the Airy equation makes \(s_3\) smooth.  The common Neumann trace at zero and the differential identity show that \(s_3'\) has a common finite trace there.  As \(|u|\to\infty\), put \(x=|u|/2-C_3\).  The cited Airy-ratio asymptotic gives on each half-line,
\[
s_3(u)=\operatorname{sign}(u)\{\sqrt{x}+O(x^{-1})\}
=\operatorname{sign}(u)\sqrt{|u|/2}+O(|u|^{-1/2}).
\]
The derivative estimates are not obtained by differentiating this remainder.  Instead the exact Riccati identity gives
\[
s_3'(u)=\frac12\{s_3(u)^2-x\}=O(|u|^{-1/2}),
\]
because \(s_3(u)^2=x+O(x^{-1/2})\).  Differentiating the exact Riccati identity on each open half-line gives
\[
s_3''(u)=s_3(u)s_3'(u)-\frac14\operatorname{sign}(u)=O(1).
\]
Thus \(s_3'\) and \(2s_3s_3'=(s_3^2)'\) are bounded outside a compact interval.  Together with half-line smoothness, the common finite trace of \(s_3'\) at zero, and compactness on bounded intervals, this proves that \(s_3'\) is bounded and Lipschitz, \(s_3^2\) is Lipschitz, and \(|s_3'(u)|\leq K(1+|u|)^{-1/2}\).

For fixed \(\eta\), the potential \(V(\cdot,\eta)\) is continuous and coercive, so the direct method gives a normalized form minimizer.  Its weak Euler equation is
\[
-4\psi''+V(\cdot,\eta)\psi=\lambda_\eta\psi.
\]
In one dimension \(H^1\) functions are continuous; the equation then implies that \(\psi'\) is continuous at \(u=\pm|\eta|/2\).  Hence the interfaces impose continuity of both the wavefunction and its first derivative, with no additional boundary term.

statements.statement:
There exist constants \(k,K>0\), independent of \(n\) and of the schedule-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D\), such that the broad complete-schedule prior satisfies
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau}
\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_{B,n}}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
\geq \frac{1+k\|\bar q(\mathcal D)-q^\star\|^2}{n}
-K n^{-9/8}.
\]
The inequality remains valid when one or more expected arm shares are zero.
statements.proof_tex:
The prior density \(w(v)=15(1-v^2)^2/16\) satisfies
\[
\int_{-1}^1\frac{w'(v)^2}{w(v)}\,dv
=\int_{-1}^1 15v^2\,dv=10.
\]
Since \(P_a=1/2+\varepsilon_nV_a\) and \(\varepsilon_n=n^{-1/4}/4\), the prior information for \(P_a\) is \(10/\varepsilon_n^2=160n^{1/2}\).  Conditional on \((P,A)\), the observations are independent Bernoulli variables, and their expected information matrix is diagonal with entry
\[
\kappa_n\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}r_a,
\qquad
\kappa_n=\mathbb E\{P_a(1-P_a)\}^{-1}=4+O(n^{-1/2}),
\]
uniformly because \(P_a\in[1/4,3/4]\).

For \(\beta(P)=\sum_ac_aP_a\), coordinatewise integration by parts and vector Cauchy--Schwarz give
\[
\inf_D\mathbb E(D-\beta)^2
\geq\sum_{a=1}^3
\frac{c_a^2}{\kappa_n\mathbb E_{\mathcal D}r_a+160n^{1/2}}.
\tag{26}
\]
The numerator is the gradient \(c\), and the denominator is the sum of likelihood and prior information.  Writing \(q=\bar q(\mathcal D)\), the scaled limit of the right side is
\[
F(q)=\frac14\sum_a\frac{c_a^2}{q_a}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
F(q)\geq\frac14\left(\sum_a|c_a|\right)^2=1,
\]
with equality only at \(q=q^\star\).  The Hessian is positive definite on the simplex tangent plane at \(q^\star\).  Compactness away from \(q^\star\), together with the positive ridge in (26), gives constants \(k_0,K_0>0\), uniformly on the closed simplex, such that
\[
\sum_a\frac{c_a^2}{\kappa_n n q_a+160n^{1/2}}
\geq\frac{1+2k_0\|q-q^\star\|^2}{n}-K_0n^{-3/2}.
\tag{27}
\]

Conditional on \(P\), \(\mathbb E\{\tau(z)\mid P\}=\beta(P)\).  Since \(\sum_ac_a=0\), the unit contrast vanishes unless \(U_i\) falls between \(\min_aP_a\) and \(\max_aP_a\), an interval of length at most \(2\varepsilon_n\).  Independence across \(i\) then implies
\[
\mathbb E\{\tau(z)-\beta(P)\}^2
\leq\frac{2\varepsilon_n}{n}=O(n^{-5/4}).
\tag{28}
\]
The \(L^2\) triangle inequality applied to (26)--(28), followed by squaring, gives
\[
\inf_D\mathbb E(D-\tau)^2
\geq\frac{1+k\|q-q^\star\|^2}{n}-Kn^{-9/8}
\]
after decreasing \(k>0\) and increasing \(K<\infty\).  The ridge denominators in (26) remain positive when some \(q_a=0\), so the conclusion includes the simplex boundary.

statements.statement:
For every \(n,M\) and every interior \(q\),
\[
0\leq\Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{all}}-G_n^{\mathrm{all}}
\leq\frac1{4M^2},
\qquad
0\leq\Lambda_{n,M}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)-G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
\leq\frac1{4M^2}.
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Restricting actions cannot lower either minimax value, proving the two left inequalities.  Conversely, for any action \(d\in[-1,1]\), choose the adjacent points \(g_-\leq d\leq g_+\) of \(\Gamma_M\) and randomize between them so that the randomized action \(G\) has mean \(d\).  Since \(g_+-g_-=1/M\),
\[
\operatorname{Var}(G)\leq\frac{(g_+-g_-)^2}{4}
=\frac1{4M^2}.
\]
For every target value \(\tau\),
\[
\mathbb E(G-\tau)^2=(d-\tau)^2+\operatorname{Var}(G)
\leq(d-\tau)^2+\frac1{4M^2}.
\]
Apply this replacement independently at each finite observation orbit \((r,x)\), and then take the same maxima and minima as in the two orbit games.  This proves both right inequalities, including cells of zero likelihood because the construction is defined on every cell.

statements.statement:
There is a neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(q^\star\) such that, for
\[
F(q)=\frac14\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\frac{c_a^2}{q_a},
\]
the following lower bounds hold.  Uniformly for \(q_n-q^\star=O(n^{-1/6})\),
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)
\geq \frac{F(q_n)}n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Uniformly for arbitrary \(q_n\in\mathcal N\) with \(q_n\to q^\star\),
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)\geq\frac{F(q_n)}n-O(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Both bounds are witnessed by explicit \(q_n\)-dependent priors on complete binary schedules.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\) near \(q^\star\) and define
\[
F=F(q),\qquad d_a=\frac{c_a}{4Fq_a}.
\]
Then
\[
\sum_ac_ad_a=1,\qquad
4\sum_aq_ad_a^2=F^{-1},
\]
and \(d\to(1/2,-1/2,-1/2)\) as \(q\to q^\star\).  Put
\[
u=1+\frac{d_3-d_2}{2},\quad
v=1+\frac{d_2-d_3}{2},\quad
e_0=-1-\frac{d_2+d_3}{2},\quad
e_1=-1+\frac{d_2+d_3}{2}.
\]
For \(\alpha>0\), assign probabilities
\[
p_{101}=u\alpha,\quad p_{110}=v\alpha,\quad
p_{000}=\frac12+e_0\alpha,\quad
p_{111}=\frac12+e_1\alpha,
\tag{4}
\]
and zero to the other types.  For \(\alpha<0\), complement every bit in the law at \(|\alpha|\).  At zero put mass \(1/2\) on each of \(000,111\).  Since \(u,v\to1\) and \(e_0,e_1\) remain bounded, (4) is a probability law for all sufficiently small \(|\alpha|\), uniformly on a fixed neighborhood of \(q^\star\).  The identities
\[
u+v=2,\quad e_0+e_1=-2,\quad
d_1=1+\frac{d_2+d_3}{2}
\]
show directly that
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha\mu(t)=\alpha,\qquad
\Pr_\alpha\{Y(a)=1\}=\frac12+d_a\alpha,\qquad
\mathbb E_\alpha\mu(t)^2=\frac{|\alpha|}{2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Draw labelled unit types independently from (4), with
\(\alpha=n^{-1/3}X\) and an even smooth compactly supported density \(f\) for \(X\).  This is an explicit prior on complete schedules, chosen after \(q\), as is permitted in a Bayes lower bound for the fixed-\(q\) minimax game.

Conditional on \((\alpha,A)\), observations are independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities in (5).  Their information for \(\alpha\) is
\[
n\sum_aq_a\frac{d_a^2}{1/4-d_a^2\alpha^2}
=\frac nF+O(n\alpha^2).
\tag{6}
\]
Let \(g_q(\alpha,A,Y)=\mathbb E_\alpha\{\tau(z)\mid A,Y\}\).  Exact binary conditioning gives
\[
g_q=\alpha+\frac1n\sum_i
\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_\alpha(\mu,Y(A_i))}
     {\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(Y(A_i))}
\{Y_i-\mathbb E_\alpha Y(A_i)\}.
\tag{7}
\]
The finite sums in (4) give, uniformly for \(q\) near \(q^\star\),
\[
\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_\alpha(\mu,Y(a))}
     {\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(Y(a))}
=B_a(q)|\alpha|+O(\alpha^2),
\quad
(B_1,B_2,B_3)=(2,d_2-d_3,d_3-d_2).
\tag{8}
\]
Define \(H(q)=\sum_aq_ad_aB_a(q)\).  Then \(H\) is continuous and
\[
H(q^\star)=\frac12.
\tag{9}
\]
Differentiating (7) on the two half-lines and averaging at the true parameter yields
\[
\mathbb E_\alpha(\partial_\alpha g_q)
=1-H(q)|\alpha|+O(\alpha^2).
\tag{10}
\]
Here are the hypotheses needed to import the generalized Van Trees step from \(\textnormal{lem:label-preserving-bayes-expansion}\).  Let \(\varpi_n(\alpha)=n^{1/3}f(n^{1/3}\alpha)\), with \(f\) smooth and compactly supported inside the interval on which (4) is a probability law.  Conditional on the assignment vector, the likelihood is a finite product of Bernoulli likelihoods with probabilities \(1/2+d_a\alpha\); for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly for \(q\) in the fixed neighborhood, these probabilities stay strictly between zero and one on the support of \(\varpi_n\).  Hence the likelihood and \(g_q\) are differentiable on each open half-line and the joint prior-likelihood score is square-integrable.  The compact support of \(f\) makes the outer boundary terms vanish.  Equation (7), together with the \(O(|\alpha|)\) regression coefficient in (8), shows that \(g_q\) has the same trace from the two sides at zero; the likelihood has the same trace as well.  Splitting integration by parts at zero therefore produces equal and opposite inner boundary terms, so there is no cusp contribution.  With these hypotheses verified, the integration-by-parts identity and Cauchy--Schwarz inequality proved in \(\textnormal{lem:label-preserving-bayes-expansion}\) apply.  Equations (6) and (10), followed by \(\alpha=n^{-1/3}X\), give
\[
\inf_D\mathbb E(D-g_q)^2
\geq
\frac Fn-n^{-4/3}
\{F^2I(f)+2FH(q)m_1(f)\}+O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{11}
\]
By (5), the conditional residual variance contributes
\[
\frac12m_1(f)n^{-4/3}+O_f(n^{-5/3})
\]
with a positive sign to the risk; the variance explained in (7) is \(O(\alpha^2/n)\).  Consequently
\[
\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
\geq \frac Fn-n^{-4/3}
\left[F^2I(f)+\{2FH(q)-1/2\}m_1(f)\right]
+O_f(n^{-5/3}).
\tag{12}
\]

If \(q-q^\star=O(n^{-1/6})\), then \(F\to1\) and \(H(q)\to1/2\), uniformly on compact scaled sets.  Choose even smooth compactly supported densities approaching \(\phi_3^2\).  The Airy variational identity gives
\[
I(f)+\frac12m_1(f)\longrightarrow C_3.
\]
A diagonal choice whose cutoff grows sufficiently slowly makes the remainder in (12) uniform and proves the first assertion.  For the second assertion, keep one fixed compactly supported \(f\); continuity of \(F\) and \(H\) bounds the bracket in (12) on \(\mathcal N\), giving the stated \(O(n^{-4/3})\) lower bound.

statements.statement:
At the global minimax-value level needed for the sharp expansion, the exact eight-type binary orbit game yields matching bounds without deleting zero-likelihood cells or dormant primal constraints.  The Airy-feedback rule satisfies
\[
\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D_{q^\star},\delta_{n,q^\star};z)
\leq n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\]
uniformly over complete schedules, while the allocation-regularized complete-schedule prior \(\Pi_n\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau}\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_n}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z)
\geq n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\]
uniformly over every schedule-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D\).  Consequently the unrestricted and iid \(q^\star\) global minimax values have the same displayed second-order expansion.  This theorem asserts only these global worst-case/Bayes value inequalities.  It does not establish a uniform liminf or recovery comparison over an \(\eta\)-band, a transverse-stratum comparison, or cellwise Le Cam equivalence; those stronger claims remain open in \(\textnormal{oeq:uniform-singular-bridge}\).
statements.proof_tex:
The exact orbit proposition holds for every integer \(n\) and retains every zero-count and zero-likelihood observation cell.  The upper half of \(\textnormal{prop:matching-finite-n-constructions}\) gives the first displayed inequality uniformly over all complete binary schedules.  Its proof depends on a schedule only through \(x=n^{1/3}\tau(z)\) and \(A_n=n^{-2/3}\sum_i\mu(t_i)^2\), using \(A_n\geq|x|/2\); therefore it covers edge endpoints, outgoing directions, and macroscopic departures without discarding constraints.

The lower half of the same proposition uses actual priors on complete labelled schedules.  Its half-effect component concentrates on \(\eta=0\), while \(\textnormal{lem:broad-prior-coercivity}\) makes the Bayes lower bound uniform over every schedule-independent assignment law.  The grid-randomization bound transfers both inequalities to finite rational games within \(1/(4n^2)=o(n^{-4/3})\), with an action defined on every finite observation cell.  Maximizing risk dominates averaging under \(\Pi_n\), and unrestricted design includes iid \(q^\star\); sandwiching yields the common global minimax-value expansion.

Nothing in this argument constructs fiberwise dual recovery away from \(\eta=0\) or a uniform experiment comparison over \(|\eta|\leq\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{bridge}}\).  The Airy fiber calculus identifies the minimizing fiber and its trace conditions, but it does not supply the stronger transverse comparison.  That distinction is recorded by leaving \(\textnormal{oeq:uniform-singular-bridge}\) open.

statements.statement: In the balanced two-arm binary finite-population problem, the minimax risk of the reduced shifted-binomial experiment equals the minimax risk obtained by jointly optimizing over all schedule-independent assignment laws and all estimators; the reduced game has a unique minimax rule and a least-favorable-prior Bayes representation.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2.1. r_n*=ρ_n*=inf_f sup_{I_n} E(f(p+Bin(r,1/2))−(p−q)/n)². Moreover, there is a unique f_n* minimizing (6) and it is the posterior mean of (p−q)/n under a least-favorable prior π_n* on I_n. As a consequence, f_n* is admissible and ρ_n* is the Bayes risk of π_n*. Theorem 2.2. Let f_n* be the function minimizing (6) in the reduced model. Then inf_{A,τ̂} sup_{P∈{0,1}²ⁿ} R_n(A,τ̂)=ρ_n*.

statements.statement: In the published two-arm finite-population problem, for every finite \(L<U\), the unrestricted minimax squared-error risk over schedules in \([L,U]^{2n}\) is exactly \((U-L)^2\) times the binary minimax risk, and a conditional Bernoulliization of the binary minimax rule attains that value.

statements.statement:
Fix \(n\geq1\) and finite constants \(L<U\), and put \(W=U-L\).  For every schedule-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D\), without any positivity or independence restriction on its coordinates,
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}}
\sup_{z^{[L,U]}\in[L,U]^{3n}}
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau_{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]})
=W^2\inf_{\widehat\tau}
\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z).
\]
Consequently the exact finite-\(n\) equalities
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}=W^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}},
\qquad
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=W^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)
\]
hold for every interior \(q\).  Together with the binary orbit reduction they imply
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}=W^2G_n^{\mathrm{all}},
\qquad
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q)=W^2G_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q).
\]
The last two equalities identify minimax values only: the eight-type kernel \(P_m(x\mid r)\) is not asserted to be a literal orbit likelihood for nonendpoint bounded schedules.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\), \(L<U\), a schedule-independent \(\mathcal D\), and set \(W=U-L>0\).  We first hold \(\mathcal D\) fixed.

For any clipped bounded rule \(d\) and binary schedule \(z=(t_i)_{i=1}^n\), set \(Y_i^{[L,U]}(a)=L+Wt_{i,a}\).  Since \(\sum_ac_a=0\),
\[
\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]})
=\frac1n\sum_{i,a}c_a(L+Wt_{i,a})=W\tau(z).
\tag{29}
\]
The normalized rule
\[
d^{\mathrm{bin}}((A_i,t_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n)
=W^{-1}d((A_i,L+Wt_{i,A_i})_{i=1}^n)
\]
is measurable and lies in \([-1,1]\).  Equation (29) gives
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,d;z^{[L,U]})
=W^2R_n(\mathcal D,d^{\mathrm{bin}};z).
\]
Endpoint schedules form a subset of \([L,U]^{3n}\), so
\[
\inf_d\sup_{z^{[L,U]}}R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,d;z^{[L,U]})
\geq W^2\inf_{\widehat\tau}\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}
R_n(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau;z).
\tag{30}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix a clipped binary rule \(e\) and a bounded schedule.  Put
\[
p_{i,a}=\frac{Y_i^{[L,U]}(a)-L}{W}\in[0,1].
\]
Independently of \(A\), generate conditionally independent \(B_i(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{i,a})\), and define
\[
d_e(A,Y^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}})
=W\,\mathbb E_B\left[
e((A_i,B_i(A_i))_{i=1}^n)\mid A,Y^{[L,U],\mathrm{obs}}
\right].
\tag{31}
\]
The conditional expectation depends on the fixed bounded schedule only through the observed probabilities \(p_{i,A_i}\), so (31) is an observed-data rule.  Convexity gives values in \([-W,W]\).  Moreover, by zero-sum of \(c\),
\[
\mathbb E_B\tau(B)
=\frac1n\sum_{i,a}c_ap_{i,a}
=W^{-1}\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]}).
\tag{32}
\]
Conditional Jensen applied to \(e(A,B^{\mathrm{obs}})-\tau(B)\) yields
\[
\left\{d_e-W\mathbb E_B\tau(B)\right\}^2
\leq W^2\mathbb E_B\left[
\{e(A,B^{\mathrm{obs}})-\tau(B)\}^2\mid A,z^{[L,U]}
\right].
\tag{33}
\]
Taking expectation over \(A\), interchanging the finite expectations, and using schedule independence of \(\mathcal D\),
\[
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,d_e;z^{[L,U]})
\leq W^2\mathbb E_BR_n(\mathcal D,e;B)
\leq W^2\max_{z\in\mathcal T^n}R_n(\mathcal D,e;z).
\tag{34}
\]
Taking the bounded-schedule supremum and then the infimum over \(e\) proves the reverse of (30).  Thus the fixed-design equality is exact.  Infimizing over the identical schedule-independent design class gives the unrestricted equality; fixing \(\mathcal D_q\) gives the iid equality.  Finally, \(\textnormal{prop:imported-eight-type-orbit-infrastructure}\) yields the two orbit-value identities.  The auxiliary averaging in (31)--(34) proves only equality of minimax values, not a literal eight-type representation of a nonendpoint schedule.
statements.justification: The theorem proves exact fixed-design and minimax equalities using endpoint inclusion and a valid Rao--Blackwellized observed-data rule.
statements.gap: It generalizes the published two-arm endpoint transfer to the present zero-sum three-arm contrast and unrestricted schedule-independent design class.
statements.consumer: Every binary sharp expansion, allocation comparison, estimator, and lower prior can be transported to a common bounded interval with the correct squared-width scaling.

statements.statement:
Fix finite endpoints \(L<U\), independent of \(n\), and put \(W=U-L\).  At \(q=q^\star\), the Rao--Blackwellized estimator \(\delta_{n,q^\star}^{[L,U]}\) satisfies
\[
\sup_{z^{[L,U]}\in[L,U]^{3n}}
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D_{q^\star},\delta_{n,q^\star}^{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]})
\leq W^2\left\{\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\right\}.
\]
The rescaled endpoint prior \(\Pi_n^{[L,U]}\) satisfies, uniformly over every schedule-independent assignment law \(\mathcal D\),
\[
\inf_{\widehat\tau_{[L,U]}}
\mathbb E_{z^{[L,U]}\sim\Pi_n^{[L,U]}}
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,\widehat\tau_{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]})
\geq W^2\left\{\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\right\}.
\]
Thus both bounded procedures are explicit finite-\(n\) maps or priors, and no exact finite-\(n\) saddle attainment is asserted.
statements.proof_tex:
The upper bound in \(\textnormal{prop:matching-finite-n-constructions}\) holds for \(\delta_{n,q^\star}\).  Apply the Rao--Blackwell construction in \(\textnormal{def:bounded-endpoint-constructions}\) with this binary rule.  Inequality (34) from \(\textnormal{thm:bounded-outcome-endpoint-transfer}\) gives
\[
\sup_{z^{[L,U]}}R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D_{q^\star},
\delta_{n,q^\star}^{[L,U]};z^{[L,U]})
\leq W^2\left\{\frac1n-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\right\}.
\]

For the lower construction, \(\Pi_n^{[L,U]}\) is supported on endpoint schedules.  Given any bounded rule \(d\), normalize its restriction to endpoint data as in the lower-bound part of the endpoint-transfer proof, obtaining a clipped binary rule \(d^{\mathrm{bin}}\).  The pushforward definition and (29) give
\[
\mathbb E_{z^{[L,U]}\sim\Pi_n^{[L,U]}}
R_{n,[L,U]}(\mathcal D,d;z^{[L,U]})
=W^2\mathbb E_{z\sim\Pi_n}R_n(\mathcal D,d^{\mathrm{bin}};z).
\]
Taking the infimum over \(d\) and applying the binary prior lower bound proves the second display uniformly in \(\mathcal D\).  Since \(0<W<\infty\) is fixed, multiplication by \(W^2\) preserves the order \(o(n^{-4/3})\).

statements.statement:
For fixed finite endpoints \(L<U\), with \(W=U-L\), the bounded three-arm minimax values obey
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}
=\frac{W^2}{n}-W^2C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),
\qquad
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)
=\frac{W^2}{n}-W^2C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Consequently
\(\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)-\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}=o(n^{-4/3})\).  After normalization by \(W^2\), the half-wedge spectral value remains exactly \(C_3=-a_1'\).
statements.proof_tex:
For every \(n\), \(\textnormal{thm:bounded-outcome-endpoint-transfer}\) gives
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}=W^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{all}},
\qquad
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star)=W^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q^\star).
\]
Substitute the two expansions in \(\textnormal{thm:sharp-face-corner-expansion}\).  Because \(W\) is fixed, finite, and positive, \(W^2o(n^{-4/3})=o(n^{-4/3})\).  Subtraction gives the risk-gap assertion.  Division by \(W^2>0\) shows that normalization leaves the dimensionless spectral value \(C_3=-a_1'\) unchanged.  This transport uses only the proved global minimax-value expansion and makes no use of the open fiberwise singular comparison.

statements.statement:
Let fixed finite endpoints \(L<U\) have width \(W=U-L\), and let \(q_n\to q^\star\).  Uniformly whenever \(\zeta_n=n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\) ranges over a compact subset of the simplex tangent plane,
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)
=\frac{W^2}{n}+W^2n^{-4/3}\{\mathsf P(\zeta_n)-C_3\}
+o(n^{-4/3}).
\]
Thus the bounded iid array retains the unrestricted bounded sharp correction if and only if
\(n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\to0\).  If \(q_n\to q^\star\) and
\(n^{1/6}\|q_n-q^\star\|\to\infty\), then
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-W^2/n\right\}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
The allocation threshold is unchanged and its risk penalty is multiplied by \(W^2\).
statements.proof_tex:
For every \(n\), endpoint transfer gives
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)
=W^2\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n).
\tag{35}
\]
Multiply the uniform expansion from \(\textnormal{thm:local-allocation-frontier}\) by the fixed constant \(W^2\).  Its remainder remains \(o(n^{-4/3})\), uniformly on the same compact subsets, proving the displayed bounded expansion.  Because \(W^2>0\), equation (35) preserves the necessary-and-sufficient condition for matching the unrestricted sharp correction.  Finally,
\[
n^{4/3}\left\{\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-W^2/n\right\}
=W^2n^{4/3}\left\{\rho_n^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)-1/n\right\},
\]
so the binary divergence conclusion implies the bounded one.  The endpoint identity therefore transports the already-proved binary frontier without invoking any stronger singular-experiment comparison.

statements.statement:
On the bounded restricted schedule class
\(Y_i^{[L,U]}(2)=Y_i^{[L,U]}(3)\) for every \(i\), pooling labels \(2\) and \(3\) under \(q^\star\) produces balanced two-arm assignment and the causal target becomes the active-arm mean minus the pooled-comparator mean.  The endpoint subclass is represented by the published shifted-binomial experiment, while the entire bounded pooled problem has minimax risk \(W^2\) times that binary value.  Its second-order deficit coefficient is therefore \(W^2(-4^{1/3}a_1')\).  This is a value transfer; \(P_m(x\mid r)\) is not a literal likelihood for a nonendpoint bounded schedule.
statements.proof_tex:
Write the common comparator outcome as \(Y_i^{[L,U]}(0)\).  Since \(q_1^\star=1/2\) and \(q_2^\star+q_3^\star=1/2\), pooling labels \(2,3\) maps \(\mathcal D_{q^\star}\) to iid balanced two-arm assignment.  The split between the two pooled labels is ancillary because their potential outcomes agree, and
\[
\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]})
=\frac1n\sum_i\{Y_i^{[L,U]}(1)-Y_i^{[L,U]}(0)\}.
\]
On endpoint schedules, normalization by \(W>0\) gives the balanced binary two-arm problem.  The declared published experimental-reduction result identifies its minimax value with the shifted-binomial value, the declared published endpoint-transfer result gives the exact multiplier \(W^2\) for the full bounded problem, and the declared sharp-constant result gives binary coefficient \(-4^{1/3}a_1'\).  Hence the bounded coefficient is \(W^2(-4^{1/3}a_1')\).  Because endpoint transfer averages binary endpoint experiments, it establishes a value identity and does not turn a nonendpoint bounded schedule into an eight-type orbit.
